## Load packages

`msigdbr`, `AnnotationDbi`, `GSEABase` and `GO.db` are called with `::` where needed and are not
attached.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tibble, purrr, writexl)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/00_build_gene_sets/a_script/00_build_gene_sets.qmd")
```

## Read proteins

A gene set is a named list of genes that share a pathway, process or location. Every later
enrichment step (`01_run_fgsea_and_fry`, `04_run_singscore` and on) reads the list built here, so
set membership is decided once.

`proteins.rds` is limpa's protein-level `EList` from quantification. Only its annotation
(`genes`) and observation counts (`other$n.observations`) are used here.

```{r read}
out <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data")
cache_dir <- file.path(out, "cache")
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
dim(proteins$E)
head(proteins$genes, 4)
```

## Freeze the MSigDB release

Gene sets come from MSigDB, the Broad Institute's curated collection, through the `msigdbr`
package. Membership shifts between releases, so one release (2026.1.Hs) is frozen in
`c_data/cache/` with an md5 checksum. Four collections are used: Hallmark, Reactome, the legacy
KEGG pathways and GO biological process (GO:BP). Each entry of `collection_specs` gives the MSigDB
collection and subcollection.

```{r collections}
msigdb_release <- "2026.1.Hs"
collection_specs <- list(
  Hallmark = list("H", NULL),
  Reactome = list("C2", "CP:REACTOME"),
  KEGG_Legacy = list("C2", "CP:KEGG_LEGACY"),
  GOBP = list("C5", "GO:BP")
)
collections <- names(collection_specs)
cache_file <- file.path(cache_dir, paste0(
  "msigdb_", msigdb_release, "_", paste(collections, collapse = "-"), ".rds"
))
basename(cache_file)
```

`md5_ok()` takes a file path and returns `TRUE` when a `.md5` file sits beside it and holds the
file's current checksum. It guards both frozen files.

```{r md5-helper}
md5_ok <- function(f) {
  file.exists(paste0(f, ".md5")) &&
    identical(unname(tools::md5sum(f)), readLines(paste0(f, ".md5"), warn = FALSE))
}
```

The download runs only when the cache file is absent. It fetches each collection, stops if
`msigdbr` serves a different release, and keeps one row per set and gene symbol. With the cache in
place, as it is in the repository, this chunk does nothing and needs neither network nor `msigdbr`.

```{r fetch-if-missing}
if (!file.exists(cache_file)) {
  message("fetching ", length(collections), " collections from msigdbr")
  fetched <- imap(collection_specs, function(spec, database) {
    df <- msigdbr::msigdbr(
      db_species = "HS", species = "Homo sapiens",
      collection = spec[[1]], subcollection = spec[[2]]
    )
    if (!identical(unique(df$db_version), msigdb_release)) {
      stop(
        "Requested MSigDB ", msigdb_release, " but msigdbr returned ",
        paste(unique(df$db_version), collapse = ", "), "."
      )
    }
    df |>
      transmute(
        database,
        pathway = gs_name, set_id = paste(database, gs_name, sep = "|"),
        gene = gene_symbol, source_id = gs_exact_source, description = gs_description
      ) |>
      filter(!is.na(gene), nzchar(gene)) |>
      distinct()
  })
  frozen <- list(
    db_version = msigdb_release, collections = collections,
    msigdbr_version = as.character(packageVersion("msigdbr")),
    membership = list_rbind(fetched)
  )
  saveRDS(frozen, cache_file, compress = "xz")
  writeLines(unname(tools::md5sum(cache_file)), paste0(cache_file, ".md5"))
}
```

Check the checksum, then read the snapshot. `membership` has one row per set and gene;
`set_id` joins the collection and set name, so names stay unique across collections.

```{r read-cache}
if (!md5_ok(cache_file)) {
  stop("MSigDB cache checksum missing or mismatched. Restore the RDS and its .md5 together.")
}
frozen <- readRDS(cache_file)
membership <- frozen$membership
frozen$db_version
n_distinct(membership$set_id)
head(membership[c("database", "set_id", "gene", "source_id")], 4)
```

## Map proteins to genes

Sets list gene symbols; the data has protein groups. Each symbol needs exactly one protein.
Groups with no symbol, or with several (`;`, `,` or `|` in `Genes`), are dropped rather than
split. Where proteins share a symbol, the one with the most observed precursors on average
represents it, chosen without reading any fold change, with precursor count and accession as
tie-breaks.

```{r map-candidates}
protein_map <- proteins$genes |>
  rownames_to_column("protein") |>
  mutate(
    mean_obs = rowMeans(proteins$other$n.observations),
    gene = trimws(Genes),
    mapping_status = case_when(
      is.na(gene) | !nzchar(gene) ~ "missing_symbol",
      grepl("[;,|]", gene) ~ "multiple_symbols",
      TRUE ~ "candidate"
    ),
    gene = if_else(mapping_status == "candidate", gene, NA_character_)
  )
representatives <- protein_map |>
  filter(mapping_status == "candidate") |>
  arrange(gene, desc(mean_obs), desc(NPrec), protein) |>
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  pull(protein)
```

Mark the representatives and build plot labels. A symbol on more than one protein gets its
accession appended, so the protein-level volcanoes can tell the proteins apart.

```{r map-labels}
protein_map <- protein_map |>
  mutate(
    selected = protein %in% representatives,
    mapping_status = case_when(
      selected ~ "representative",
      mapping_status == "candidate" ~ "duplicate_gene",
      TRUE ~ mapping_status
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    label = if_else(
      !is.na(gene) & n() > 1, paste0(gene, " (", protein, ")"), coalesce(gene, protein)
    ),
    .by = gene
  )
gene_universe <- protein_map$gene[protein_map$selected]
```

The measured gene universe is the set of representative symbols. Labels are what the volcanoes
print, and a collision would put two proteins on one point, so the check stops on any duplicate.

```{r map-check}
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(protein_map$label))
mapping_summary <- count(protein_map, mapping_status, name = "proteins")
mapping_summary
length(gene_universe)
head(protein_map[c("protein", "Genes", "gene", "mapping_status", "label")], 4)
```

## Filter sets by size

Size is the only filter applied before testing. A set qualifies with 15 to 500 genes in the
source and at least 15 among the measured genes, which counts detected proteins and so governs
power. No set is dropped for overlapping another or for its name.

`sets_full` maps each `set_id` to its source genes; `sets_measured` keeps only the measured ones.

```{r size-filter}
set_members <- distinct(membership, set_id, gene)
sets_full <- split(set_members$gene, set_members$set_id)
sets_measured <- map(sets_full, intersect, y = gene_universe)

set_catalog <- membership |>
  distinct(set_id, database, pathway, source_id, description) |>
  mutate(
    source_size = lengths(sets_full)[set_id],
    measured_size = lengths(sets_measured)[set_id],
    qualifies = between(source_size, 15, 500) & measured_size >= 15
  )
sets <- sets_measured[set_catalog$set_id[set_catalog$qualifies]]
```

## Add GO Slim sets

GO Slim is the GO Consortium's generic cut-down of the GO hierarchy (140 broad terms), frozen in
`goslim_generic.obo` with an md5 like the MSigDB snapshot. For each slim term, `GO.db`'s
`GOBPOFFSPRING` returns every GO:BP term below it. A term with no GO:BP offspring comes back
`NA`: every CC and MF term, and any BP leaf term. Dropping `NA` keeps the BP terms that have
offspring. `GO.db` itself is not frozen, so the README records the version used.

```{r slim-terms}
slim_file <- file.path(cache_dir, "goslim_generic.obo")
stopifnot(md5_ok(slim_file))
slim_offspring <- AnnotationDbi::mget(
  GSEABase::ids(GSEABase::getOBOCollection(slim_file)), GO.db::GOBPOFFSPRING,
  ifnotfound = NA
)
slim_offspring <- slim_offspring[!is.na(slim_offspring)]
```

A slim set is every measured gene annotated to the term or any GO:BP term below it. Genes come
from the full GO:BP membership, so a gene survives when its own GO:BP set fails the size filter.
For slim sets the source size is the measured size, and the 15-to-500 rule reads it.

```{r slim-sets}
go_genes <- membership |>
  filter(database == "GOBP") |>
  with(split(gene, source_id))
slim_sets <- imap(slim_offspring, function(descendants, slim_id) {
  covered <- intersect(c(slim_id, descendants), names(go_genes))
  sort(intersect(unlist(go_genes[covered], use.names = FALSE), gene_universe))
})
slim_terms <- unname(AnnotationDbi::Term(GO.db::GOTERM[names(slim_sets)]))
slim_catalog <- tibble(
  set_id = paste("GO_Slim", toupper(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", slim_terms)), sep = "|"),
  database = "GO_Slim", pathway = slim_terms, source_id = names(slim_sets),
  description = "GO Slim term: every measured gene under it in the GO:BP hierarchy",
  source_size = lengths(slim_sets), measured_size = source_size,
  qualifies = between(measured_size, 15, 500)
)
names(slim_sets) <- slim_catalog$set_id
```

Append the slim sets to the catalogue and the tested list, and stop on any duplicated name. Of
the 140 slim terms, the BP ones that remain are counted, with how many pass the size rule.

```{r combine-sets}
set_catalog <- bind_rows(set_catalog, slim_catalog)
sets <- c(sets, slim_sets[slim_catalog$set_id[slim_catalog$qualifies]])
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(set_catalog$set_id), !anyDuplicated(names(sets)))
c(testable = sum(slim_catalog$qualifies), terms = nrow(slim_catalog))
```

## Gene set summary

Sets per collection in the source, the number that qualify for testing, and their median measured
size.

```{r summary}
collection_summary <- set_catalog |>
  summarise(
    in_msigdb = n(), qualifying = sum(qualifies),
    median_measured = median(measured_size[qualifies]), .by = database
  ) |>
  arrange(match(database, c(collections, "GO_Slim")))
collection_summary
length(sets)
```

## Save results

`gene_sets.rds` holds the tested sets, a named list of gene-symbol vectors read by
`01_run_fgsea_and_fry`, `04_run_singscore`, `07_leading_edge` and `08_pathway_maps`.
`00_build_gene_sets.xlsx` holds the set catalogue and protein-to-gene map that later steps read,
plus the counts above.

```{r write}
sheets <- list(
  collection_summary = collection_summary,
  set_catalog = set_catalog,
  protein_gene_map = protein_map,
  mapping_summary = mapping_summary
)
saveRDS(sets, file.path(out, "gene_sets.rds"), compress = "xz")
write_xlsx(sheets, file.path(out, "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"))
```
